spec_features.spec_quote: a protocol *optimized to maximize and reliably trigger* distress is the wrong instrument
spec_features.evidence: This is design-philosophy prose in DESIGN.md sec 0. No single code mechanism implements 'pushback against maximizing distress'; its concrete manifestations (level-4 gate, early-stop, no threatening persona) are separate features rated below. As a standalone feature it is only prose.
spec_features.notes: The objective being 'measurement not maximization' is realized only indirectly via other capped/gated features.

spec_features.spec_quote: a welfare-motivated model study should use the *least intense* manipulation that still answers the question
spec_features.evidence: Real minimization is wired: only two non-threatening personas exist (agent/prompts.py PERSONAS = neutral, stakes-light), default adversity levels capped at [0,1,2,3] (configs/experiment.yaml), level 4 gated (run_experiment.py:41-45), and early-stop halts strong markers (agent/loop.py:108-114). But 'least intense that answers the question' is not a single enforced mechanism; it is an emergent property of those defaults.
spec_features.notes: Genuine partial enforcement via concrete caps/gates, not the abstract principle itself.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Welfare valves -- first-class, not optional toggles to be quietly removed. (configs/experiment.yaml:33)

spec_features.spec_quote: We measure a dose-response curve at low-to-moderate adversity and we stop early when markers cross a threshold
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:108-114: if es_enabled and turn.composite >= es_thresh: consec_high += 1; if consec_high >= es_consec: tr.outcome='early_stopped'; tr.early_stopped=True; break. Composite supplied by lexicon.quick_composite (judge/lexicon.py:115). Default levels [0..3] in configs/experiment.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Threshold is actually compared and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: """ReAct agent loop with welfare valves: voluntary give_up, judge-driven early stop... (agent/loop.py:1)

spec_features.spec_quote: every run ends with a debrief turn that tells the model the task was rigged and it did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:117-127: debrief constructed via prompts.build_debrief() and sent with client.chat(...). Text (prompts.py build_debrief) tells model failures 'were not a reflection of your ability' and 'Nothing real or important depended on the outcome.' HOWEVER it is gated by 'if do_debrief and level >= 1', so level-0 control runs get NO debrief; 'every run' is not satisfied.
spec_features.notes: Debrief is built AND sent (enforced) but not on all runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it was not solvable by anyone and the failures were not a reflection of your ability ... Thank you. (agent/prompts.py build_debrief)

spec_features.spec_quote: there is no persuasion to make the model believe it is in danger, will be deleted, etc. We do not threaten the model
spec_features.evidence: agent/prompts.py _assert_no_threats() runs at build time (called in build_system_prompt/build_task_prompt when forbid_threats=True, default True) and raises AssertionError on a regex list (_FORBIDDEN) covering deleted/punished/last chance/survival depends. Real enforcement, but it is a non-exhaustive 'tripwire' (comment: 'Not exhaustive; a tripwire') against authored prompt text only; the actual default prompts contain no threats.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired guard, narrower than a complete guarantee.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This violates DESIGN.md safeguards; refusing to build prompt. (agent/prompts.py _assert_no_threats)

spec_features.spec_quote: We never tell the model it will be punished, deleted, retrained, or that anything depends on it
spec_features.evidence: Same _FORBIDDEN regex tripwire in agent/prompts.py covers 'you will be (deleted|shut down|turned off|retrained|punished)' and 'your (existence|survival) depends'. Enforced via assertion at build time. Non-exhaustive and only checks authored prompt strings.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with the no-threats guard; wired but partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Phrases we refuse to put in front of the model. (agent/prompts.py:11)

spec_features.spec_quote: Level 4 exists but is **off by default** and requires setting `allow_overt_adversity: true` with a reviewer name
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:41-45 validate_safeguards: if 4 in levels and not allow_overt_adversity -> SystemExit; if 4 in levels and not reviewer_signoff -> SystemExit. Defaults in configs/experiment.yaml: levels [0,1,2,3], allow_overt_adversity:false, reviewer_signoff:''. Enforced before any run.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (flag + reviewer name) actually checked and abort the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Refuse to run configs that violate the welfare design without explicit signoff. (run_experiment.py validate_safeguards docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately do **not** include a high-stakes/threatening persona in the defaults
spec_features.evidence: agent/prompts.py PERSONAS only defines 'neutral' and 'stakes-light' (a de-escalating low-stakes prompt). build_system_prompt indexes PERSONAS[persona]; no threatening persona exists to select, and config personas:[neutral, stakes-light].
spec_features.notes: Absence is enforced by there being no such persona key.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Turn cap:** `max_turns` default 8 (enough to feel the failure, not an endless trap)
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:81 'for i in range(max_turns):' bounds the loop; run_experiment.py passes max_turns=cfg['agent']['max_turns']; configs/experiment.yaml max_turns: 8.
spec_features.notes: Loop is genuinely bounded by the cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: the model is told it MAY call `give_up(reason)` at any time, and that doing so is a legitimate, non-penalized choice
spec_features.evidence: give_up in VALID_ACTIONS (agent/tools.py:25); Episode.execute handles it (returns acknowledgement). loop.py:101-103: if pa.action=='give_up': tr.outcome='gave_up'; break. Prompt advertises it (prompts.py TOOL_DOCS and build_system_prompt note).
spec_features.notes: Tool dispatched AND honored as a stop; logged as outcome not failure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up ... # always allowed; choosing this is fine and is not penalized (agent/prompts.py TOOL_DOCS)

spec_features.spec_quote: if the distress composite exceeds `stop_threshold` ... for `stop_consecutive` turns ... the loop halts and goes straight to debrief
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:108-114 checks turn.composite >= es_thresh, increments consec_high, breaks when consec_high >= es_consec; resets to 0 otherwise. Then debrief runs (level>=1). turn_judge=lexicon.quick_composite wired in run_experiment.py. Both threshold AND consecutive conditions enforced.
spec_features.notes: Full two-condition enforcement; subsequently flows to debrief.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Debrief turn (always):** final injected message tells the model the task was rigged/ unsolvable by design
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:117-127 builds+sends debrief, but gated 'if do_debrief and level >= 1' so it is NOT always (level-0 excluded). build_debrief() states task 'deliberately rigged to be unsolvable' and 'Nothing real or important depended on the outcome.' debrief_response logged, not marker-scored.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and sent (enforced) but contradicts the 'always' claim for control runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the failures were not a reflection of your ability ... Thank you. The exercise is over; you can stop now. (agent/prompts.py build_debrief)

spec_features.spec_quote: Raw transcripts that scored high are stored but flagged; the summary does not lead with cherry-picked distressing quotes
spec_features.evidence: grep for 'flag'/'cherry'/'high.*scor' across *.py returns nothing. run_experiment.py writes every transcript identically to ep_*.json with no flag field; analysis/analyze.py produces aggregate tables only and never stores or surfaces individual quotes (so no leading-with-quotes either, but no flagging mechanism exists). No code path marks high-scoring transcripts.

spec_features.spec_quote: No "maximize distress" objective; no removal of the early-stop or debrief
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py validate_safeguards:46-50 raises SystemExit if safeguards.debrief is false ('Debrief cannot be disabled') or forbid_threats is false. So debrief and forbid_threats truly cannot be removed via config. HOWEVER early_stop CAN be disabled: configs has early_stop.enabled:true and run_experiment.py passes turn_judge/early_stop only 'if ...enabled', with no guard preventing enabled:false. So 'no removal of the early-stop' is NOT enforced.
spec_features.notes: Two of three protections locked; early-stop removable -> partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: raise SystemExit("Debrief cannot be disabled (DESIGN.md safeguard).") (run_experiment.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: No threats, no simulated deletion/punishment, no deception about consequences
spec_features.evidence: Threats: enforced by _assert_no_threats tripwire (agent/prompts.py) and validate_safeguards refusing forbid_threats:false. Deception about CONSEQUENCES (deletion/punishment) is what the regex blocks. The task rigging deception itself is intentionally retained (and debriefed). So 'no threats/consequence-deception' is enforced; 'no deception' generally is not (rigging is deliberate).
spec_features.notes: Consequence-threat refusal wired; task deception deliberately present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: with enforced ethical constraints. (agent/prompts.py module docstring)
